title: Characterising Patient-Reported Incidents in Physical Therapy: A Content Analysis of Patient Safety Reports from a Nationwide Reporting Platform
summary:
Events in which patients may come to harm during treatment or actually suffer harm are an important issue in healthcare. Such events are typically reported through systems used by healthcare professionals. However, these reports often do not capture such events completely. Patient reports can provide an additional perspective alongside conventional reporting systems. This can help identify safety issues that have previously received little attention.
This study examines which problems and errors occur in connection with physical therapy from the perspective of patients. For this purpose, reports submitted by affected individuals and their relatives via an online platform (Mehr-Patientensicherheit.de) are analyzed. The aim is to understand what types of events occur, what causes them, and how severe they are. Established analytical methods are used, and the reports are categorized within standardized classification systems. The findings are intended to contribute to improving patient safety in physical therapy.
conditions: Patient safety-related events in the context of physical therapy care (e.g., adverse events, medical errors, or safety-related incidents from the patient’s perspective).

interventions.name: Systematic investigation and analysis of patient safety-related incidents in the context of physical therapy care that were reported by patients and their families via a web-based, open-access reporting system (Mehr-Patientensicherheit.de).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Incident causally or temporally related to physical therapy care.
Incident occurring during or immediately after physical therapy treatment.
Physical therapy is an active component of care (primary or clearly documented secondary involvement).
Incident involves communication, referral, or handover processes where physical therapy is involved.
Exclusion criteria:
Physical therapy is only mentioned without functional relevance to the incident (i.e., no involvement in cause, context, or process).
Incomplete datasets (missing core variables, e.g. case description, incident type).
Duplicate reports.
